title: Your First 24 Hours in Medina, Dealt as Cards
description: A ten-stop first day that begins at Medina’s spiritual center, reads the city through prayer grounds, museums and battle landscapes, pauses over regional cooking, and closes at Quba.

cards.title: The Prophet’s Mosque
cards.subtitle: Daybreak anchor
cards.notes: Begin quietly in the mosque and its courtyards. This is a place of worship associated with the Prophet’s life and companions, so let prayer and local etiquette set the pace.
cards.short_summary: Start where the Prophet built his mosque after arriving in Medina; later expansions have carried the complex through successive eras.

cards.title: The Prophet’s Mosque Museum
cards.subtitle: Read the building
cards.notes: Use the models and multilingual presentations to decode the pulpit, mihrab, domes, gates and successive expansions before encountering those elements elsewhere.
cards.short_summary: The museum documents more than 1,400 years of the mosque’s architecture through visual, written and audio material.

cards.title: Al-Ghamamah Mosque
cards.subtitle: Trace the old prayer ground
cards.notes: Notice the basalt, white lime and sequence of domes. The structure marks part of Al-Musalla, where the Prophet led Eid and rain-invoking prayers.
cards.short_summary: This mosque preserves one of the prayer sites in the former open ground southwest of the Prophet’s Mosque.

cards.title: Chefs Market
cards.subtitle: First substantial meal
cards.notes: Choose by appetite rather than trying to survey every counter. The documented range includes mandi, madhbi, kebab, Kabuli and Bukhari rice, manto and yaghmush.
cards.short_summary: A long-established food complex brings numerous traditional restaurants and cuisines from across the Islamic world into one market.

cards.title: Al-Qiblatain Mosque
cards.subtitle: Locate a turning point
cards.notes: Give this stop one focused question: how does a building hold the memory of a changed direction? The mosque commemorates the shift of the qibla toward the Kaaba.
cards.short_summary: Its name and identity are tied to the 2 AH event in which the direction of Muslim prayer changed from Jerusalem to Mecca.

cards.title: The Seven Mosques
cards.subtitle: Read the trench landscape
cards.notes: Look beyond the collective name: the official account explains that five small historic mosques remain here and that the label “Seven Mosques” developed later.
cards.short_summary: The group stands at the foot of Mount Sila’, near the setting of the Battle of the Trench.

cards.title: Uhud Martyrs Square
cards.subtitle: Set the battle in terrain
cards.notes: Use Mount Uhud, Archers’ Hill and the martyrs’ cemetery as three reference points. The terrain makes the official account of the battle’s changing course easier to follow.
cards.short_summary: The square gathers major landmarks associated with the Battle of Uhud, including the mountain, Archers’ Hill and the cemetery of the martyrs.

cards.title: Dar Al-Madinah Museum
cards.subtitle: Reassemble the city
cards.notes: Shift from outdoor sites to models, photographs, manuscripts and architectural material. The exhibits connect the Prophet’s biography with Medina’s changing urban form.
cards.short_summary: The museum preserves Medina’s Islamic and architectural heritage through dedicated halls, models, images and historical collections.

cards.title: Hijaz Railway Museum
cards.subtitle: Add the rail-era layer
cards.notes: Study the surviving station buildings and railway material as evidence of how pilgrims once entered Medina from Damascus and points farther north.
cards.short_summary: The restored terminal station now presents the Hijaz Railway alongside galleries covering Medina from the pre-Islamic period to the modern era.

cards.title: Quba Mosque
cards.subtitle: Close with the migration story
cards.notes: End with worship or quiet observation. Quba returns the day to the Prophet’s arrival in Medina and the foundation of the first mosque in Islam.
cards.short_summary: The mosque was founded after the Prophet’s migration and remains connected to the Prophet’s Mosque by the Quba walking trail.
